protocol: Explicit two-stage experimental procedure, not a drop-in one-call prompt. Three independent four-candidate plans per original source; an external seeded uniform draw selects one candidate per plan before any content is reviewed. Expand only that candidate with the neutral-biography final-record recipe. No previous run or rejected draft is fed into later independent trials. All plans and selections are retained. The candidate distribution is model-defined, not population-calibrated.

variants.hypothesis: Separating proposal generation from selection may prevent the model from repeatedly choosing its own familiar default when asked to consider alternatives internally.

operations.new:
## Generation Rules

This request is the planning stage of a fictional-person generator. Instead of choosing a single default biography, describe four distinct possible individuals, each independently satisfying all the supplied particulars. An external random draw will select one of these four for a later full specification. Do not rank the possibilities, select a favorite, merge them, or give one a preferred survey response.

Each possibility must be a coherent life, not a bundle of demographic stereotypes or a slogan. Make the differences consequential to everyday life, relationships and the requested interests. A different city or job title alone is not a different life. Do not make all four variations of one career-and-vacation template. They may share ordinary preferences without being copies of each other.

Describe people rather than advising them. Avoid manufacturing virtues, defects or unusual tastes to fill a quota. The supplied traits do not specify a whole psychological profile. There is no requested attitude toward prices, luxury, technology, risk or a future survey offer. Choose the open details freely, without treating one demographic category as having a single correct way to live.

Return only a JSON object with a "candidates" array containing exactly four objects. Each object must contain these fields:

- "particulars": explicit name, age, gender, nationality, race_ethnicity, residence, gross household income, partnership status, children status, political identification and requested reading interest. Every original constraint must be satisfied by every candidate.
- "life_course": a concise account of education, work or retirement, household and the experiences leading to the current situation.
- "daily_life": social commitments, chosen activities and ordinary routines.
- "travel": desired experiences, companions, feasible time and resources, and one concrete past choice or experience. Leave any later product decision open.
- "personality_and_voice": recognizable tendencies, speech and behavior. Describe fictional choices, not measured psychological results.

Use enough detail to distinguish the lives and check their coherence, roughly 200-300 words per candidate. These sketches are fictional alternatives, not facts about one shared person. The requested name is used in each alternative; it does not mean they share a biography.

Do not invent external geography, scheduled-event dates or locations, precise current service prices or institutional rules. Personal experiences may be fictional; external facts are not. Keep future arrangements undecided when necessary.

This is a way to explore possibilities. Equal selection among these model-generated candidates does not imply equal real-world prevalence or a representative population sample.
